title: Modular failover and locality routing for reranker endpoint
creator: Rina Kapoor
description: Problem: The reranker service experiences tail-latency spikes and region-specific degradations during traffic surges and infra maintenance. Current fallback behavior is coarse: full-service fallback to a lower-capacity region or returning cached top-k which can hurt quality. Goal: introduce a modular, runtime-configurable failover stack that supports per-customer affinity, progressive degradation (score-preserving soft-degrades), circuit breakers with graded actions, and region-aware routing policies so that we can meet P99 latency SLOs while preserving rerank quality where possible.
acceptance_criteria: Add a runtime-configurable circuit-breaker component that supports 3 action tiers: (1) continue with slower region but cache-prefetch, (2) soft-degrade by returning top-K from base embedding scores plus minimal rerank when latency permits, (3) hard-fallback to cached response. Configurable per-route and per-customer
Introduce regional affinity weights and a policy engine so requests prefer local region, then warm-prefetch remote candidate sets asynchronously before failover triggers
Implement deadline-aware short-circuit: requests with remaining headroom <= X ms trigger a lighter rerank path that only rescoring top-10 candidates
End-to-end integration tests that simulate cross-region outage and validate <1% quality regression (nDCG@10) for Tier-1 customers during staged failovers
Dashboard exposing circuit-breaker state counts, per-region fallbacks, P50/P95/P99 latency slices and quality regression alerts
tasks: Design: failover stack spec and policy language (PM + Eng) - Confluence doc - in progress
Runtime: implement circuit-breaker library with graded actions and metrics emittance - PR#4567
Routing: add regional affinity weights and policy evaluation in gateway/router - PR#4580
Rerank path: add deadline-aware light-rescore path (top-10 only) and ensure KV cache reuse
Testing: load tests with geo-failure injection and quality evaluation against eval-suite-v2
Console: add new panels for failover traces and per-customer fallback counts
design_decisions: Use token-based deadlines propagated from edge so downstream components can choose light vs full path
Prefer asynchronous prefetch of remote candidate sets while initial local scorer runs to reduce cold-fallback latency
Circuit-breaker tripping based on a combination of recent P99 latency and error rate, with gradual ramp-down instead of hard close
Per-customer profiles: default policy is conservative for free-tier (more aggressive fallback) and permissive for enterprise (try more retries/regions)
Store policy configs in Config Service v3 so ops can change without deploy
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: increased complexity could introduce routing loops. Mitigation: implement max-hops and an idempotent fallback flag in request metadata
Risk: quality regressions during soft-degrade. Mitigation: require canary on <5% traffic and run nDCG/eval harness before full rollout
Risk: metrics volume increase from circuit-breaker states. Mitigation: sample events at 10% and emit aggregated counters
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): enable per-route circuit-breaker on internal staging region for 5% traffic (2 days)
Phase 1: expand to 25% with enterprise customers opted-in; monitor nDCG, latency, and error surface (3 days)
Phase 2: global enable with gradual weight tuning and ops runbook for manual override (1 week)
Rollback: controller button to pin old routing and disable prefetch; metrics-driven automatic rollback if P99 latency rises >20% or nDCG drops >3% for >30m
test_plan: Unit tests for circuit-breaker state transitions and policy parsing
Integration tests: simulate region outage and assert fallback path triggers and response correctness
Load tests: k6 script simulating 100k rps across 4 regions with injected 30s blackout on one region
Quality tests: run eval-suite-v2 nightly with seeded prompts and compare nDCG@10 against baseline
